qe: The Third Round Table Conference, which directly contributed to the formulation of the Government of India Act 1919 updates, was convened in November 1932. Which significant political entity completely abstained from its proceedings?
qh: नवंबर 1932 में आयोजित तीसरा गोलमेज सम्मेलन, जो भारत सरकार अधिनियम के निर्माण में सहायक बना, में किस महत्वपूर्ण राजनीतिक संस्था ने पूरी तरह से दूरी बनाए रखी थी?
o: The Indian National Congress
The All India Muslim League
The National Liberal Foundation
The Hindu Mahasabha
e: Detailed Explanation: The Third Round Table Conference was held in London in November 1932. Just like the first conference, the Indian National Congress refused to participate, as it was in the midst of the Civil Disobedience civil agitations.

qe: The British Parliament formally enacted the landmark Government of India Act in which month and year?
qh: ब्रिटिश संसद ने किस महीने और वर्ष में ऐतिहासिक भारत सरकार अधिनियम (Government of India Act) को आधिकारिक रूप से पारित किया था?
o: August 1935
November 1932
December 1929
March 1942
e: Detailed Explanation: Following structural discussions across the Round Table Conferences, the British Parliament formally passed the comprehensive Government of India Act in August 1935.

qe: According to the blueprints of the 1935 legislation, the proposed All India Federation was designed to encompass which administrative components?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के खाके के अनुसार, प्रस्तावित अखिल भारतीय महासंघ (All India Federation) में कौन से प्रशासनिक घटक शामिल होने थे?
o: All British Indian provinces, all chief commissioner’s provinces, and the Indian princely states
The three presidency coastal towns of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras exclusively
The central Imperial Legislative Council zones combined solely with Burma
Only the autonomous states that possessed a separate legal currency registry
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1935 provided for an All India Federation that would dynamically combine all British Indian provinces, all chief commissioner’s provinces, and the sovereign Indian states (princely states) under a single statutory umbrella.

qe: The integration of the Princely States into the proposed 1935 All India Federation was conditional upon them securing what minimum seat threshold within the proposed Council of States?
qh: प्रस्तावित 1935 के अखिल भारतीय महासंघ में रियासतों का शामिल होना उनके द्वारा प्रस्तावित राज्य परिषद (Council of States) में न्यूनतम कितनी सीटों के आवंटन को स्वीकार करने पर निर्भर था?
o: 52 seats
260 seats
141 seats
30 seats
e: Detailed Explanation: The formation of the federation was strictly conditional on princely states being allotted a total minimum of 52 seats inside the upper house (Council of States) agreeing to join the framework.

qe: Apart from legislative seat counts, what demographic condition was mandatory for the princely states to fulfill before the All India Federation of 1935 could be operationalized?
qh: विधायी सीटों के अलावा, 1935 के अखिल भारतीय महासंघ के चालू होने से पहले रियासतों के लिए किस जनसांख्यिकीय शर्त (demographic condition) को पूरा करना अनिवार्य था?
o: The aggregate population of the joining states had to be 50 per cent of the total population of all Indian states
They had to represent exactly 78 million Bengali-speaking residents across territories
The landless agricultural laborers within those states had to possess universal voting rights
Their combined population tracking metric had to match the urban middle classes of Bombay Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: A key hurdle for the federation was that the aggregate population of the princely states opting to join had to constitute at least 50 per cent of the total collective population of all native Indian states.

qe: Because the princely states refused to fulfill the strict population and seat conditions, the All India Federation never materialized. How did the central government of India continue to operate up to 1946?
qh: चूंकि रियासतों ने जनसंख्या और सीट की शर्तों को पूरा करने से इनकार कर दिया, इसलिए अखिल भारतीय महासंघ कभी अस्तित्व में नहीं आया। इसके कारण भारत की केंद्र सरकार 1946 तक किस अधिनियम के तहत काम करती रही?
o: As per the administrative and executive provisions of the Government of India Act, 1919
Under the unilateral emergency ordinances issued by the Secretary of State based in London
According to the temporary regulatory guidelines introduced by the Metcalfe Act of 1835
As a complete military protectorate directed by the British War Cabinet exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Since the required number of princely states defaulted on joining, the federal part of the 1935 Act remained a dead letter. Consequently, the central executive architecture of India continued to function all the way up to 1946 under the older provisions of the Government of India Act 1919.

qe: Which centralized administrative authority was explicitly designated as the absolute 'pivot' of the entire constitutional machinery under the Government of India Act, 1935?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 के तहत किस केंद्रीकृत प्रशासनिक प्राधिकारी को पूरे संवैधानिक तंत्र का पूर्ण 'धुरी' (pivot) नामित किया गया था?
o: The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Federal Assembly
The Secretary of State for India
The Chief Justice of the Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The statutory structure of the 1935 Act concentrated ultimate executive authority in one position, making the Governor-General the undisputed pivot of the entire Constitution.

qe: Under the federal executive division of the 1935 Act, which specific portfolio heads were categorized as 'Reserved Subjects' to be managed exclusively by the Governor-General?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के संघीय कार्यकारी विभाजन के तहत, किन विशिष्ट विभागों को 'आरक्षित विषयों' (Reserved Subjects) के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया था, जिनका प्रबंधन विशेष रूप से गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा किया जाना था?
o: Foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs
Education, health, local self-government, and land revenue tracking
Customs tariffs, currency valuation, and corporate textile protection metrics
Law and order, public finance, and mass technical industrial education
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act divided administrative portfolios into two bands. The critical 'Reserved Subjects' comprised foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs, keeping them under the exclusive control of the Governor-General.

qe: How did the constitutional position of the Executive Councillors who advised the Governor-General on 'Reserved Subjects' differ from that of popular ministers?
qh: आरक्षित विषयों पर गवर्नर-जनरल को सलाह देने वाले 'कार्यकारी पार्षदों' (Executive Councillors) की संवैधानिक स्थिति लोकप्रिय मंत्रियों से किस प्रकार भिन्न थी?
o: They were completely insulated from legislative oversight and were not responsible to the central legislature
They were elected directly via universal adult franchise across all British provinces
They were legally forced to resign if the lower house passed a vote of no-confidence
They were subordinated to the popular ministers headed by a provincial premier
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act maintained a non-democratic core at the center. The executive councillors who managed the reserved portfolios were bureaucratic nominees who were explicitly not responsible or answerable to the central legislature.

qe: Under the 1935 Act, the 'Transferred Subjects' at the federal level were to be administered by the Governor-General on the advice of ministers who faced which constitutional condition?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत, संघीय स्तर पर 'हस्तांतरित विषयों' (Transferred Subjects) का प्रशासन गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा उन मंत्रियों की सलाह पर किया जाना था, जिन्हें किस संवैधानिक शर्त का सामना करना पड़ता था?
o: They were responsible to the federal legislature and were legally forced to resign on losing its confidence
They were nominated directly by the Chamber of Princes based on population strength
They held permanent, lifetime tenures that were completely insulated from any legislative vote
They were paid entirely out of the British exchequer in London to prevent economic drain
e: Detailed Explanation: Ministers who managed the Transferred subjects were elected members chosen from the legislature. They were constitutionally responsible to the federal legislature and had to resign if they lost the confidence of that legislative body.

qe: What executive parameter allowed the Governor-General to completely bypass ministerial advice and act independently under his own authority under the 1935 Act framework?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत किस कार्यकारी नियम ने गवर्नर-जनरल को मंत्रिस्तरीय सलाह को पूरी तरह से दरकिनार करने और स्वतंत्र रूप से काम करने की अनुमति दी थी?
o: Acting in his individual judgement for the discharge of his special responsibilities regarding security and tranquillity
Securing a direct judicial warrant signed by three judges panel of the High Court
Filing a written petition cleared by a majority of the provincial elected premiums
Invoking the historical maritime navigation rules passed during Wellesley's administration
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act armed the Governor-General with wide discretionary limits. He was statutorily authorized to act under his own 'individual judgement' to fulfill his special responsibilities for safeguarding the security and tranquillity of India.

qe: The central bicameral legislature designed by the Government of India Act, 1935, was composed of which two houses?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 द्वारा तैयार की गई केंद्रीय द्विसदनीय विधायिका किन दो सदनों से मिलकर बनी थी?
o: The Council of States (upper house) and the Federal Assembly (lower house)
The House of Representatives (lower house) and the Senate (upper house)
The Central Legislative Assembly and the Imperial Advisory Board
The Chamber of Princes and the Provincial Councils division
e: Detailed Explanation: The legislative architecture at the federal level was designed to be bicameral, containing an upper chamber named the Council of States and a lower chamber named the Federal Assembly.

qe: Under the structural layout of the 260-member Council of States, what percentage of seats was reserved to be nominated directly by the princely rulers?
qh: 260 सदस्यीय काउंसिल ऑफ स्टेट्स (Council of States) के संरचनात्मक ढांचे के तहत, कितने प्रतिशत सीटें सीधे रियासतों के शासकों द्वारा मनोनीत की जानी थीं?
o: 40 per cent
One-third (33 per cent)
50 per cent
14 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: The 260 seats of the upper house were split to integrate conservative elements. While a portion was elected from British provinces, exactly 40 per cent of the total members were to be nominated directly by the princes.

qe: The lower house, or the Federal Assembly, was structured to feature 375 members. What specific fraction of this house was designated to be nominated by the native princes?
qh: निचले सदन, या फेडरल असेंबली (Federal Assembly) में 375 सदस्य होने थे। इस सदन का कितना विशिष्ट हिस्सा देशी राजकुमारों द्वारा मनोनीत किया जाना तय किया गया था?
o: One-third
Forty per cent
Half
Ten per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: To check progressive nationalist forces in the lower house, the 375-member Federal Assembly had a substantial non-elected block: exactly one-third of its total membership was to be nominated by the autocratic princes.

qe: What paradoxical structural feature characterized the election methodology fixed for the two central houses under the 1935 Act framework?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत दोनों केंद्रीय सदनों के लिए तय की गई चुनाव पद्धति की कौन सी विरोधाभासी संरचनात्मक विशेषता थी?
o: Election to the Council of States was direct, while election to the Federal Assembly was indirect
Election to both houses was based entirely on universal adult franchise tracking
The Federal Assembly members were elected directly, while the upper house was entirely nominated
Both houses relied strictly on indirect selection via local village panchayats exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Paradoxically, the 1935 Act flipped standard parliamentary norms. It introduced a direct election methodology for the upper chamber (Council of States) and an indirect election process for the lower house (Federal Assembly).

qe: What operational tenure and retirement parameters were fixed for the upper chamber (Council of States) under the 1935 Act directives?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत उच्च सदन (Council of States) के लिए कौन से परिचालन कार्यकाल और सेवानिवृत्ति के मानदंड तय किए गए थे?
o: It was a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every third year
It held a fixed non-renewable tenure of 5 years for all members simultaneously
It was subject to arbitrary dissolution by the Premier every single year
It had a continuous 7-year cycle with half of its members retiring every second year
e: Detailed Explanation: The Council of States was structured as a permanent legislative body. It was not subject to dissolution, and its stability was maintained by having one-third of its total members retire every third year.

qe: Under the legislative power schedules of the 1935 Act, which specific branch of the central legislature held the exclusive authority to move a vote of no-confidence against ministers?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के विधायी शक्ति नियमों के तहत, केंद्रीय विधायिका की किस विशिष्ट शाखा के पास मंत्रियों के खिलाफ अविश्वास प्रस्ताव लाने का विशेष अधिकार था?
o: The Federal Assembly
The Council of States
The Governor's Executive Board
The Chamber of Princes
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act distributed powers unequally between the chambers. Only the members of the lower house (Federal Assembly) were armed with the power to move a vote of no-confidence against ministers, while the Council of States held no such power.

qe: What extraordinary financial parameter illustrates the complete lack of legislative sovereignty over public finance under the 1935 central legislative framework?
qh: कौन सा असाधारण वित्तीय पैमाना 1935 के केंद्रीय विधायी ढांचे के तहत सार्वजनिक वित्त पर विधायी संप्रभुता की पूर्ण कमी को दर्शाता है?
o: Exactly 80 per cent of the total central budget remained completely non-votable
The legislators were entirely barred from discussing any land revenue items
The entire public finance framework had to be cleared by the London exchequer manually
Indian ministers held zero authority to ask any supplementary financial questions
e: Detailed Explanation: Although parliamentary forms were displayed, the central legislature's control over expenditure was blocked: exactly 80 per cent of the total federal budget remained entirely non-votable by the members.

qe: The 1935 legislative framework split powers into three lists: federal, provincial, and concurrent. Who was legally endowed with the ultimate 'residuary powers' of legislation?
qh: 1935 के विधायी ढांचे ने शक्तियों को तीन सूचियों (संघीय, प्रांतीय और समवर्ती) में विभाजित किया। कानून बनाने की अंतिम 'अवशिष्ट शक्तियाँ' (residuary powers) कानूनी रूप से किसे प्रदान की गई थीं?
o: The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Federal Assembly
The British Parliament in London directly
The Premier heading the Council of Ministers
e: Detailed Explanation: In the federal legislative mapping of lists, any residual subject that was not explicitly noted inside the three charts was placed under the authority of the Governor-General.

qe: Apart from residuary powers, what overriding financial authority did the Governor-General hold regarding budget allocations inside the central legislature?
qh: अवशिष्ट शक्तियों के अलावा, केंद्रीय विधायिका के भीतर बजट आवंटन के संबंध में गवर्नर-जनरल के पास कौन सा सर्वोपरि वित्तीय अधिकार सुरक्षित था?
o: He held the sovereign power to restore cuts in grants executed by the legislature
He could completely liquidate all corporate tax deposits to clear the public debt
He held the right to levy an automatic 50% tariff surcharge on native khadi workshops
He was legally forced to route 100% of his financial decisions to the Constituent Assembly
e: Detailed Explanation: The Governor-General retained a strong grip over public finance. Even if the legislature voted to cut or reduce specific financial grants, he held the overriding power to restore those cuts to protect colonial interests.

qe: Under the structural shifts introduced in the third section of the 1935 Act, what system formally replaced the unworkable framework of 'Dyarchy' at the provincial level?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तीसरे खंड में शुरू किए गए संरचनात्मक बदलावों के तहत, प्रांतीय स्तर पर 'द्वैध शासन' (Dyarchy) के अव्यवहारिक ढांचे के स्थान पर कौन सी प्रणाली औपचारिक रूप से लागू की गई थी?
o: Provincial Autonomy
Bicameral Federalism
Centralized Direct Rule
Saptanga Decentralization Mappings
e: Detailed Explanation: At the provincial level, the 1935 Act introduced a significant structural change: it completely abolished the dual-rule system of Dyarchy and replaced it with 'Provincial Autonomy'.

qe: Following the introduction of Provincial Autonomy, how was the statutory legal relationship between the provinces and the central authorities modified?
qh: प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता की शुरुआत के बाद, प्रांतों और केंद्रीय अधिकारियों के बीच वैधानिक कानूनी संबंध को कैसे संशोधित किया गया था?
o: Provinces were freed from the superintendence of the Governor-General and derived legal authority directly from the British Crown
Provinces were completely subordinated to a specialized three-judge panel of the central assembly
The provincial administrations lost their separate legal identities and financial powers completely
Provinces were legally forced to route all their legislative codes to the Federal Assembly Speaker
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the autonomy model, provinces were granted a separate legal identity. They were formally freed from the administrative 'superintendence and direction' of both the Secretary of State and the Governor-General, deriving their legal authority directly from the British Crown.

qe: What independent financial power was granted to the provincial governments to sustain their autonomous administrative structure under the 1935 framework?
qh: 1935 के ढांचे के तहत प्रांतीय सरकारों को अपने स्वायत्त प्रशासनिक ढांचे को बनाए रखने के लिए कौन सी स्वतंत्र वित्तीय शक्ति प्रदान की गई थी?
o: The independent power to borrow money on their own security
The absolute right to print independent regional paper currencies without central guidelines
The power to levy a flat 100% transit custom tariff on all incoming British textile shipments
Complete control to reallocate 80% of the central budget grants to local village boards
e: Detailed Explanation: To provide financial backing to autonomy, provinces were given independent financial powers and resources, which explicitly included the right to borrow money directly on their own security.

qe: Under the provincial executive guidelines of the 1935 Act, the Governor was designated as the nominee and representative of which authority?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रांतीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, राज्यपाल को किस प्राधिकारी का नामांकित व्यक्ति और प्रतिनिधि नामित किया गया था?
o: The British Crown
The Central Legislative Assembly majority
The Congress Working Committee executive panel
The Chief Justice of the newly consolidated Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: The provincial executive was headed by the Governor, who was explicitly designated as the Crown's direct nominee and representative, exercising executive authority on the King's behalf within that province.

qe: What extraordinary administrative power did the provincial Governor retain under the 1935 Act if he deemed that local governance had broken down?
qh: यदि प्रांतीय राज्यपाल को लगता था कि स्थानीय शासन विफल हो गया है, तो 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत उसके पास कौन सा असाधारण प्रशासनिक अधिकार था?
o: He could completely take over and indefinitely run the provincial administration under his own authority
He had the right to petition the Federal Assembly to dissolve the British Cabinet in London
He could automatically liquidate all corporate land assets held by the local zamindars
He was legally forced to surrender his entire council to the popular ministerial premiers
e: Detailed Explanation: The Governor held wide emergency powers. If local governance broken down, he could use his special powers to completely take over and indefinitely run the entire provincial administration under his own authority.

qe: Under the provincial legislative updates of the 1935 Act, how were the members of the local provincial legislatures to be chosen?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के प्रांतीय विधायी सुधारों के तहत, स्थानीय प्रांतीय विधानसभाओं के सदस्यों का चयन कैसे किया जाना था?
o: All members were to be directly elected via an expanded franchise framework
They were to be indirectly filtered through a multi-layered tier of local body sieves
One-third were elected, while the remaining majority was nominated by the Chamber of Princes
They were handpicked by the executive councillors of the central Governor-General directly
e: Detailed Explanation: Reversing the indirect system attached to the center, the provincial legislatures were structured on democratic lines where all members were to be directly elected by the population under an expanded franchise.

qe: Regarding the administration of local affairs, the provincial subjects were to be managed by ministers in a Council of Ministers headed by which official?
qh: स्थानीय मामलों के प्रशासन के संबंध में, प्रांतीय विषयों का प्रबंधन मंत्रियों द्वारा एक मंत्रिपरिषद में किया जाना था, जिसका प्रमुख कौन सा अधिकारी होता था?
o: A Premier
The Governor-General
The Speaker of the Assembly
The Chief Commissioner
e: Detailed Explanation: Under provincial autonomy, elected ministers were responsible for administering all provincial subjects within a coordinated council of ministers, which was headed by a popular leader designated as the Premier.

qe: What financial parameter illustrates that provincial autonomy remained restricted under the 1935 Act public finance framework?
qh: कौन सा वित्तीय पैमाना यह दर्शाता है कि 1935 के अधिनियम के सार्वजनिक वित्त ढांचे के तहत प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता सीमित बनी रही?
o: Exactly 40 per cent of the provincial budget was still kept non-votable
The provincial legislatures were completely barred from passing any tax laws
The entire provincial revenue collection had to be sent to the center within a week
Indian ministers held zero authority to allocate funds for health and education
e: Detailed Explanation: Control over the purse remained constrained even at the provincial level: exactly 40 per cent of the total provincial budget was kept non-votable, maintaining bureaucratic insulation.

qe: The retrospective evaluation of the 1935 Act highlights that its narrow franchise guidelines enfranchised approximately what percentage of the total British Indian population?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम का पूर्वव्यापी मूल्यांकन यह दर्शाता है कि इसके संकीर्ण मताधिकार दिशानिर्देशों ने कुल ब्रिटिश भारतीय आबादी के लगभग कितने प्रतिशत को मताधिकार दिया था?
o: 14 per cent
50 per cent
70 per cent
2 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: Although the franchise was extended to wider sections and women got rights on the same basis as men, the qualifications remained restrictive, enfranchising a mere 14 per cent of the total British Indian population.

qe: What negative socio-political consequence did nationalist economic and political analysts attribute to the consolidation and extension of communal electorates under the 1935 Act?
qh: राष्ट्रवादी आर्थिक और राजनीतिक विश्लेषकों ने 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत सांप्रदायिक निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों के सुदृढ़ीकरण और विस्तार के लिए कौन सा नकारात्मक सामाजिक-राजनीतिक परिणाम जिम्मेदार माना?
o: It systematically promoted separatist tendencies which ultimately culminated in the partition of India
It successfully established a secular, classless society based on original democratic loops
It eliminated the dependency of local legislatures on the arbitrary vetoes of the Governor-General
It completely blocked the political standing of the conservative Aligarh school intellectuals
e: Detailed Explanation: The extension of communal and interest-based electorates under the 1935 framework deeply fractured the national fabric. Nationalists pointed out that it institutionalized divisions and promoted separatist tendencies that ultimately culminated in the partition of India.

qe: According to structural critiques, why did the Government of India Act 1935 function as a 'rigid constitution' with zero internal capacity for natural growth?
qh: संरचनात्मक आलोचनाओं के अनुसार, भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1935 ने प्राकृतिक विकास के लिए शून्य आंतरिक क्षमता के साथ एक 'कठोर संविधान' (rigid constitution) के रूप में क्यों काम किया?
o: The absolute right of constitutional amendment was reserved exclusively with the British Parliament
It gave the lower Federal Assembly absolute sovereign authority to alter any clause at will
The Act was legally forced to undergo a total public referendum across provinces every single year
It completely froze any future legislative changes from being passed by provincial councils
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act provided no mechanism for internal constitutional development. It was exceptionally rigid because the absolute right to amend or alter its provisions was kept exclusively in the hands of the British Parliament in London.

qe: From the perspective of long-term British colonial strategy, what was the primary political objective behind introducing the 1935 constitutional reforms?
qh: दीर्घकालिक ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक रणनीति के दृष्टिकोण से, 1935 के संवैधानिक सुधारों को पेश करने के पीछे प्राथमिक राजनीतिक उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To weaken the national movement and integrate large segments of it into the colonial, administrative structure
To prepare a rapid administrative blueprint for transferring complete absolute sovereignty immediately
To completely eliminate the political influence of conservative loyalists and big landlords
To consolidate all regional trade unions into an independent anti-imperialist mass front
e: Detailed Explanation: The British recognized that long-term suppression was unsustainable. Their strategic goal behind the reforms was to weaken the intensity of the national movement by co-opting and integrating large segments of the leadership into the colonial constitutional and administrative network.

qe: The British strategists believed that once nationalist Congressmen entered office and tasted administrative power under the 1935 Act framework:
qh: ब्रिटिश रणनीतिकारों का मानना था कि एक बार जब राष्ट्रवादी कांग्रेसी पद संभाल लेंगे और 1935 के अधिनियम के ढांचे के तहत प्रशासनिक शक्ति का स्वाद चख लेंगे, तो:
o: They would become highly reluctant to go back to the challenging politics of sacrifice
They would immediately launch an armed mass revolution to seize the central executive council
They would completely liquidate all existing zamindari land revenue collection systems inside provinces
They would unify into a single integrated leftist bloc to crush the Moderate liberals
e: Detailed Explanation: A calculated aspect of the British strategy was psychological. They anticipated that once Congress leaders experienced the perks and authority of administrative power, they would be reluctant to abandon office and return to the challenging, self-denying politics of sacrifice.

qe: How did British policy-makers intend to utilize the provincial autonomy provisions to create deep organizational dissensions within the Indian National Congress high command?
qh: ब्रिटिश नीति-निर्माता भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के उच्च कमान के भीतर गहरे संगठनात्मक मतभेद पैदा करने के लिए प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता के प्रावधानों का उपयोग कैसे करना चाहते थे?
o: By placating the right wing through constitutional concessions while using police measures to crush the radical leftists
By transferring the entire public finance portfolio exclusively to the control of the radical leftists
By legally forcing all Congress leaders to register their personal property assets inside London labs
By completely banning the Moderate liberals from contesting any provincial council elections
e: Detailed Explanation: The reforms were weaponized to split the nationalist front. The strategy aimed to satisfy and placate the conservative Right Wing of the Congress through constitutional concessions, while isolating and using police measures to crush the radical Leftists.

qe: British colonial authorities calculated that granting provincial autonomy would create powerful local leaders. What strategic impact did they expect this to have on the Congress?
qh: ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक अधिकारियों ने गणना की थी कि प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता देने से शक्तिशाली स्थानीय नेता पैदा होंगे। वे उम्मीद करते थे कि इसका कांग्रेस पर क्या रणनीतिक प्रभाव पड़ेगा?
o: The Congress would be provincialised and its centralized national leadership would get weakened
The central leadership would integrate tightly into an unstoppable anti-imperialist mass front
The Congress would immediately dissolve its provincial committees to form a single central cabinet
It would force the complete alignment of the party with the All India Muslim League core objectives
e: Detailed Explanation: The British calculated that provincial autonomy would turn local leaders into independent centers of political power. This would successfully 'provincialise' the Congress, distracting them with regional issues and effectively weakening the authority of the centralized national leadership.

qe: Which prominent colonial official candidly admitted the true strategic motive of the reforms by stating: 'We framed the Act of 1935 because we thought that was the best way...of maintaining British influence in India.'?
qh: किस प्रमुख औपनिवेशिक अधिकारी ने सुधारों के वास्तविक रणनीतिक उद्देश्य को स्पष्ट रूप से स्वीकार करते हुए कहा था: 'हमने 1935 का अधिनियम इसलिए बनाया क्योंकि हमने सोचा था कि भारत में ब्रिटिश प्रभाव को बनाए रखने का यह सबसे अच्छा तरीका है।'?
o: Viceroy Lord Linlithgow
Secretary of State Samuel Hoare
Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald
Viceroy Lord Irwin
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Linlithgow, who served as the Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943, documented the underlying imperial intent, admitting that the 1935 Act was engineered primarily to safeguard and maintain British influence over the sub-continent.

qe: In his analytical critique of the 1935 Act, the constitutional historian B.R. Tomlinson observed that the entire process of constitutional advance in India was determined by what colonial need?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम की अपनी विश्लेषणात्मक आलोचना में, संवैधानिक इतिहासकार बी.आर. टॉमलिंसन (B.R. Tomlinson) ने उल्लेख किया कि भारत में संवैधानिक प्रगति की पूरी प्रक्रिया किस औपनिवेशिक आवश्यकता से निर्धारित थी?
o: The need to attract Indian collaborators to the Raj
The urgent requirement to completely eliminate the economic drain of capital
The absolute necessity to introduce universal adult franchise across all colonies
The strategic goal of building up a highly sophisticated native steel industry
e: Detailed Explanation: B.R. Tomlinson's analysis exposed the co-optation model of the colonial state, noting that British constitutional concessions were structurally designed to attract and secure Indian collaborators to sustain the Raj's administrative existence.

qe: While the Indian National Congress unanimously rejected the 1935 Act, which political organizations declared themselves in favor of working its provisions at both the central and provincial levels?
qh: जबकि भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने सर्वसम्मति से 1935 के अधिनियम को खारिज कर दिया, किन राजनीतिक संगठनों ने इसके प्रावधानों को केंद्रीय और प्रांतीय दोनों स्तरों पर लागू करने (working the act) के पक्ष में घोषणा की थी?
o: The Hindu Mahasabha and the National Liberal Foundation
The Communist Party of India and the active trade unions
The All India Kisan Sabha and the Congress Leftist Faction
The radical student leagues and the Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: Breaking away from the radical rejectionist path of the Congress, both the Hindu Mahasabha and the National Liberal Foundation declared themselves in favor of participating in and working the machinery of the 1935 Act at all levels.

qe: Rejecting the unrepresentative 1935 Act framework, what alternative constitutional demand did the Indian National Congress aggressively present to the colonial state?
qh: अप्रतिनिधिक 1935 के अधिनियम के ढांचे को खारिज करते हुए, भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने औपनिवेशिक राज्य के सामने कौन सी वैकल्पिक संवैधानिक मांग आक्रामक रूप से रखी थी?
o: The convening of a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise to frame a constitution
The immediate legal restoration of the dual-rule system of Dyarchy across all provinces
A complete transfer of the absolute revenue command to the non-official members of the upper house
The mandatory structural partitioning of British India into separate linguistic segments instantly
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress counter-attacked the colonial legislation by demanding that an independent Constituent Assembly, elected via universal adult franchise, must be convened to draft a sovereign constitution for a free India.

qe: A logistical coordinate charting system frames a precise right-angled triangular layout. A car leaves station O and travels 24 km North, and then changes course to drive 7 km East to reach checkpoint B. Find the absolute straight-line distance from O to B.
qh: एक वाहन स्टेशन O से निकलता है और 24 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 7 किमी जाकर चेकपॉइंट B पर पहुँचता है। O से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 25 km
31 km
28 km
30 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement tracks a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs measuring 24 km and 7 km. The direct straight-line distance represents the hypotenuse.
By applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{24^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{576 + 49} = \sqrt{625} = \mathbf{25\text{ km}}$.
